outcomes.original: Filing step: In the final two weeks before opening, subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses to play recorded music in the restaurant. What to say: Register online with ASCAP and BMI (about $300–$2,500 per year per catalog, formula-based on occupancy and music use); federal copyright law requires a blanket license to play music publicly (background music, live covers, TV with music). The licenses are effective immediately upon sign-up, so schedule this step for the final two weeks to avoid paying for months before opening.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The day range (120–300 days) and cost range ($3,100–$15,000) are for the Conditional Use Authorization and the Health Permit to Operate, the two approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted. The CUA timeline is based on the comparable case at 3224 22nd St, which took three months (about 97 days) from filing to approval in 2023, and on typical San Francisco CUA timelines of 4–10 months including pre-application meetings, environmental review, hearing scheduling, and the 30-day appeal period. The Health Permit takes 14–45 days after plan check (21–60 days) and construction. Government costs include the CUA application fee (about $3,100 for a no-construction case, CPI-adjusted annually), the DPH plan-check fee ($828–$2,207), the Health Permit application fee ($470), and the Business Registration Certificate ($55–$700). Building permit fees ($800–$15,000) are included because tenant improvements are required, though the building row status is insufficient information. Sign permit fees ($300–$1,500) are included because exterior signage is described. The timeline is to approval; two prior CUA applications at this address were withdrawn or cancelled after 2–3 years, so execution risk is high if the mezzanine triggers the second-story restaurant prohibition or if the district cap has been reached.
